Opening: the product has two systems. First, explain what the insurer portfolio is experiencing. Second, use validated actuarial assumptions to support an individual application review. The Montreal figure is a raw record-per-policy-row ratio, not an exposure-adjusted risk rate.
Observed patterns, local context, and portfolio actions.
Property profile, expected loss, price indication, human review.
The portfolio analysis engine does not make an individual quote. The underwriting workbench needs a validated classification/rating plan and insurer assumptions. Both use traceable evidence.

16 city labels → 5 canonical cities
6 claims reported before loss date
8 claim amounts missing after dedup
48 claims Open / Under Review

No earned premium by period, insured years, claim reserves / IBNR, claim expense, operating expense, reinsurance, or investment income.

Annual written premium − claim amounts ≠ profit.

Sources: supplied policies.csv and claims.csv. 4,684 policies and 862 raw claims. There are 15 exact duplicate claim records, leaving 847 unique claim IDs. Currency is not specified in the claim data. The portfolio window is 2024-11 through 2026-10.
Montreal records more Home claims per policy row
CLAIM RECORDS PER 100 HOME POLICY ROWS
115 claim records · 510 rows · 96 policies with ≥1 claim
79 claim records · 570 rows · 72 policies with ≥1 claim

Montreal mean amount: 8,268
Toronto mean amount: 8,840
Currency unspecified · reported amount, not ultimate cost
READ THIS AS A QUESTION, NOT A VERDICT
We do not know how long each policy was insured. More claim records per row may reflect exposure time, property mix, coverage, reporting, or chance.

Exact comparison from policies.csv and deduplicated claims.csv. Montreal: 115 Home claims / 510 policy rows = 22.549 claims per 100; Toronto: 79 / 570 = 13.86. Ratio = 1.629. Distinct policies with at least one claim: Montreal 96; Toronto 72. Mean reported amount: Montreal 934,271.22 / 113 non-missing? Check amount row count; based on current report mean 8,267.89. Toronto 8,840.49. Currency absent. Exposure end dates absent, so do not call this a loss frequency.
The gap is concentrated in Water Damage
Montreal: +51 Water Damage records.  Toronto: +10 Wind/Hail records. Theft is 19 vs 21 — it does not explain Montreal’s gap.
2025: 46 Montreal / 34 Toronto · 2026 to Oct 30: 65 / 44 · 2024 is too thin to compare

Claims by loss peril from supplied files after deduplication. Montréal has 79 water, 19 theft, 14 wind/hail, 3 fire; Toronto 28, 21, 24, 6. Claims by loss year: 2025 MTL 46/TOR 34; 2026 through 2026-10-30 MTL 65/TOR 44; 2024 MTL 1/TOR 0 so not interpretable. This is a decomposition, not a causal analysis.
External sources suggest mechanisms in both cities
Montreal and Toronto both cite heavy rain, overloaded sewers, basement entry points and drainage / pump protection. These are mechanisms to test.
Shared pathways do not explain the gap
The same hazards exist in both places. The portfolio has more Montreal Water claims, but no location, insured years or cause subtype to prove why.
Counts do not point to Montreal
Portfolio Home theft is 19 Montreal vs 21 Toronto. In 2024, Toronto’s overall CMA crime rate was higher; Montreal’s Crime Severity Index was slightly higher. Neither equals insured-home theft.
Canada’s climate assessment supports testing precipitation. It does not show that weather caused this portfolio’s Montreal–Toronto difference.
Every source keeps its geography, time period, outcome and limits attached.

Source notes and links: Montreal heavy-rain guidance https://montreal.ca/en/articles/protecting-your-building-heavy-rains-68382 ; Toronto basement flooding https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/water-environment/managing-rain-melted-snow/basement-flooding/ ; Statistics Canada 2024 Crime Severity Index by CMA https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250722/t004a-eng.htm (overall police-reported crime, not insured property theft); Canada’s Changing Climate Report 2026 Chapter 5 https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/science-technology/changing-climate-report-2026/cccr-chapter-5-en.html (national scale). Each source supports a testable hypothesis, not portfolio-level causation.
Run the same investigation loop for every signal
Observation · evidence citation · competing explanation · missing data · falsification test · decision · predicted measure

This is the repeatable research workflow. The app currently provides the first Montréal Home evidence ledger and a curated source set. Live, unattended crawling/LLM research is not yet connected; sources should be retrieved through an approved search provider and captured with URL, date, geography, method and limitations.

title: PART 01 · THE PORTFOLIO HAS MORE TO ASK

text: PART 01 · THE PORTFOLIO HAS MORE TO ASK
Other patterns are leads, not verdicts
143 claims · 1,205,494 reported amount · 25.5% of all recorded amount
Preventable property losses? Need property + peril + insured-years.
Does current class predict loss after exposure adjustment?
Rare / severe; too few for stable city pricing. Check event clustering.
48 open / under review · 4 older than 90 days
Could reserve or service friction be hiding? Case reserve history needed.
18-day raw median vs Team A 12 days
Case complexity/workload may explain it; compare like with like.
No dates, renewal offer or reason; this is not a cohort churn rate.

All values from supplied policies.csv and claims.csv after exact duplicate claim cleanup. Amount units/currency unspecified. Risk class, adjuster-team, and renewal observations are raw, unadjusted or status-only comparisons. See reports/Millennium Mutual insurance findings.md for further data-quality and portfolio details.
Ask for the data that separates these causes
Forms, limits, deductible, endorsements, premium earned
Cause subtype, event ID, reserves, paid / incurred development

ECCC weather
Loss date + nearest station/grid

NRCan flood layers
Screening only; not property-level truth

StatsCan housing / crime
Context only; geography may not match
Then compare like-for-like by peril, month, property mix and insured time.

Environment and Climate Change Canada historical data https://climate.weather.gc.ca/historical_data/search_historic_data_e.html. Natural Resources Canada historic flood susceptibility data is regional screening, not individual property prediction: https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/ea1384df-bf4a-4743-97bb-870dc43f8d77 and intended use https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/1074f781-85d3-4c86-bf4a-4743-97bb-870dc43f8d77 (see report for exact catalog source). Statistics Canada census profile is tract-level, not property-level: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/98-401-X. Do not use culture, ethnicity, age, mortality or hospital use as Home-loss proxies.
The action depends on what survives the test
Montreal Water Damage stays higher per insured property-year after matching
Pilot basement-water prevention; track claims, cost and customer outcomes.
The gap is one storm/event or reporting/coding difference
Improve event accumulation, claim coding or data quality — no city-wide rate jump.
The gap vanishes after tenure, property or coverage adjustment
Do not price on city label; keep the verified explanatory factors.
Ultimate loss cost exceeds earned premium after expense and credibility
Prepare a segment-level actuarial rate review, with jurisdiction approvals.
Current decision: investigate and collect exposure data. No repricing is supported by this extract.

Actions are contingent strategies, not approved actions. Loss prevention should use a controlled comparison. Pricing requires matched earned exposure, ultimate losses, expenses, stable credibility and provincial actuarial/regulatory review. The application of any regulatory rules depends on product and jurisdiction.
Profit is an expected value plus uncertainty

N ~ claim count
X ~ cost of one claim
S = X₁ + … + Xₙ

Poisson count + independent severity:
Var(S) = λ(Var(X) + E[X]²)
Earned premium − ultimate claims − LAE − operating costs − reinsurance
Average outcomes stabilize only when exposures are comparable and dependence is limited.
Storm losses move together. More policies do not erase catastrophe risk or bad assumptions.
No profit result yet: earned premium, reserves / IBNR, LAE, expenses and reinsurance are missing.

Aggregate loss S is a compound sum. For compound Poisson, E[S]=λE[X], Var(S)=λ(E[X²]) = λ(Var(X)+E[X]^2). Chebyshev bound and formula follow if finite variance and the relevant independence/variance assumptions hold. Credibility Z=N/(N+K) requires valid exposure and estimate of K (process vs between-risk variance). Sources: CAS credibility review https://www.casact.org/sites/default/files/2021-03/8_Fisher_et_al.pdf ; CIA P&C standards https://www.cia-ica.ca/app/themes/wicket/custom/dl_file.php?fid=32707&p=37243 ; NAIC glossary https://content.naic.org/glossary-insurance-terms?id=37 ; OSFI 2026 MCT https://www.osfi-bsif.gc.ca/en/guidance/guidance-library/minimum-capital-test-guideline-2026.

Before we quote,
what risk are we
actually taking?
A transparent intake and decision-support app
Risk class · loss distribution · technical price · appetite review

The second product is an application intake and underwriting workbench. It must not improvise rate classes from the current aggregate file. A licensed insurer has to supply approved rules, rates, appetite and claim assumptions. The prototype is transparent decision support, not automatic acceptance or decline.
Start with the insured property, not a guess about the person
Use the carrier’s validated, jurisdiction-approved rating rules.
Current CSV has no property feature → outcome links, so it cannot infer a class yet.
No demographic or health proxies. Ask only for data needed to insure this property.

The AMF says Quebec home premiums can depend on home characteristics and coverage, and clients should make honest declarations. AMF home insurance shopping guidance https://lautorite.qc.ca/en/general-public/insurance/home-insurance/shopping-for-home-insurance. Rating classification should be approved for the specific insurer, product, province and filing. This prototype keeps personal demographics and health fields out.
Indicated price comes from validated loss cost

λ = claims per insured property-year
E[X] = expected ultimate claim severity

Premium = (loss + expenses + reinsurance + risk load)
÷ (1 − variable expense ratio − target margin)
The current files lack insured-years and ultimate loss by property class. The app leaves price blank until the carrier supplies validated inputs.
Compare with equivalent coverage in the market. If the market price is lower, review coverage, deductible or mitigation; do not hide an expected loss deficit.
A class rate is an estimate with uncertainty—not a promise of profit on every policy.

Pricing equation uses expense and margin ratios as proportions of premium. Exact treatment of commission, reinsurance, capital load, taxes/fees and profit margin must follow insurer accounting and approved actuarial methodology. Price comparison must be apples-to-apples by limits, form, deductible, endorsements and jurisdiction. AMF Quebec consumer guide explains coverage variation and premium considerations: https://lautorite.qc.ca/en/general-public/insurance/home-insurance/shopping-for-home-insurance.
A quote is one risk inside a whole book
Prepare a price indication; underwriter verifies coverage and declarations.
Ask for missing property data or refer to a human underwriter.
Projected loss / concentration exceeds approved limits
Refer for a documented human decision under carrier rules.
Expected claims · expected losses · expected premium · expected underwriting result · variance / stress range
The system can flag “refer” or “outside approved appetite”; it does not make the final individual accept/decline decision.

Portfolio expectation depends on class mix and credible models. For heterogeneous classes, sum expected losses and variances by segment; account for event dependence, catastrophe accumulation and reinsurance. Final underwriting disposition must comply with insurer authority, consumer treatment and local rules. AMF Quebec home insurance information states no law requires an insurer to sell insurance: https://lautorite.qc.ca/en/general-public/insurance/home-insurance/shopping-for-home-insurance. That does not remove obligations to follow applicable anti-discrimination and commercial practice rules.
Learn from outcomes. Do not skip the evidence.
Watch drift, data quality, event concentration.
Keep reason, evidence and source provenance.
Human review, fairness checks, provincial rules.
1  Explain the Montreal signal   ·   2  request missing exposure   ·   3  build approved rate inputs   ·   4  keep underwriting review human

Québec AMF AI guideline (issued March/April 2026; comes into force May 1, 2027) applies to authorized insurers and expects risk-based classification, AI governance, lifecycle management, risk management, and fair treatment: https://lautorite.qc.ca/en/professionals/insurers/guidelines/use-of-models/guideline-for-the-use-of-artificial-intelligence. Quebec Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms §20.1 has an insurance-specific provision concerning age, sex or civil status; consult counsel for applicability and exceptions: https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/pdf/cs/C-12.pdf.
